questions.prompt: Which organisms are always at the first trophic level?
Producers hold 20,000 kJ. Using the 10% law, how much energy (kJ) reaches the tertiary consumer?
Why is energy flow in an ecosystem called one-way?
options: Decomposers send energy back to the Sun
Energy lost as heat cannot be used again by producers
Energy goes only from animals to plants
questions.explain: It flows from Sun to producers to consumers and escapes as heat.

questions.prompt: What would happen if all decomposers disappeared?
options: Dead matter would pile up and nutrients would not return to the soil

questions.prompt: In grass → rabbit → fox, what is the fox?
About what fraction of sunlight falling on a leaf is stored as food?
Explain why there are usually fewer tigers than deer in a forest.
questions.modelAnswer: Tigers are at a higher trophic level than deer. At each step of the food chain only about 10% of the energy is passed on; the rest is used for life processes and lost as heat. So the energy available to tigers is much less than that available to deer, and it can support only a small number of tigers.
